findings.title: Drain queued completion IPC before deciding the previous step timed out
findings.problem: Loop tests active deadline before receiving queued IPC. If step1 sends an in-time done and next-step start near120s, a controller descheduled across the old deadline kills a timely completed step without reading its done. The claim of exit/drain final auditing does not close this ordering race.
findings.independent_reproduction: Stdlib controller substitution only: start0; queued step_done finished119.99; next guardian scheduling120.01. Result physical-substep120s deadline, recv called only twice (start then BlockingIOError); queued done was never consumed. No real Linux call or worker/scientific execution.
findings.requested_change: Drain/validate pending ordered IPC before step-deadline adjudication, both after scheduling wake and at worker exit; then enforce deadline of the still-active step. Retain rejection of done whose finished>=deadline. Add deterministic timely-queued-done/new-start, late-done, missing-done and worker-exit regression cases.

findings.title: Keep unsampled resource peaks distinct from measured zero
